items.item_text: Valid California Registered Nurse License without restriction
Blood & Marrow Transplant Certified Nurse (BMTCN) or Transplantation and Cellular Therapy Certified Nurse (TCTCN) Certification
American Heart Association (AHA) or American Red Cross Basic Life Support (BLS), or UC Davis Health CPR

Within three (3) years of hire, and every three (3) years thereafter, obtain Oncology Certification or 18 continued education units (CEUs) that are oncology specific in a three-year accreditation cycle to meet the Commission on Cancer 4.2 Standard on nursing education.
Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN)
At least two (2) years of recent clinical RN experience coordinating care for patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplant, cellular therapy, or similarly complex oncology treatment.

The Transplant Coordinator 2 (TC 2) serves as a nursing resource in the care and coordination of pre-transplant, post-transplant, and cellular therapy patients. The TC 2 is responsible for clinical case management of adult and pediatric stem cell transplant and cellular therapy candidates from referral through treatment and follow-up. This role involves coordination of the interdisciplinary care delivery system under the direction of the Medical Director and in collaboration with the broader transplant and cellular therapy team. #CA-LA
70% - Transplant Evaluation &

The Transplant Coordinator 2 functions as the primary liaison among patients, families, medical staff, referring physicians, donor agencies, insurance companies, and research partners. The TC 2 applies advanced patient assessment skills and specialized knowledge in hematology, oncology, and cellular therapy to ensure safe, evidence-based, and patient-centered care. The incumbent practices independently within the scope of the Nurse Practice Act and is accountable for providing direct patient care to a diverse population across the transplant and cellular therapy continuum.
15% - Quality and Evidence-Based Practice
5% - Professional Development
Graduation from an accredited school of nursing
Commitment to excellence in patient care.
Adapts to change in a positive, professional, and productive manner.
Ability to read, write, speak, and understand the English language.
Ability to utilize medical terminology appropriately.
Knowledge of current trends in nursing.
Effective interpersonal skills.
Demonstrates accountability and professionalism
Knowledge of legal implications in clinical practice and documentation.
Knowledge of performance improvement and evidence-based practice.

Ability to assess, plan, implement and evaluate patient care, taking into consideration protective interventions, development (behavioral and physical) and physiological characteristics specific to the patients.
